setting.title: The Last Exposure
setting.premise: Bea Lindqvist invited five guests to Pine Hollow to celebrate her sixtieth birthday. On Saturday morning her vintage rangefinder camera, with Friday's undeveloped roll still inside, is gone from the great room mantel.
setting.missingItem: Bea's vintage rangefinder camera and the undeveloped roll inside it

timeline.text: Rafe drags the antique porch rocker he broke that afternoon into the woodshed. Dot watches him go.
On the dock path at sunset, Lionel climbs a stepladder to take down the carved owl decoy he wedged in the big pine last month. Bea, shooting the sunset, takes his picture.
Juno sees Lionel hurrying up from the dock path with the stepladder and a lumpy pillowcase.
Bea takes a group photo by the fire and sets the camera on the mantel. Dot has already gone up.
Lionel says goodnight and goes upstairs. Rafe follows at 11, Bea at 11:30.
Wren and Juno stop playing music and leave the great room. The camera is still on the mantel.
Juno fetches a glass of water and goes to bed.
Wren takes a video call with her girlfriend in Lisbon out on the lakeside porch.
Dot creeps down to the kitchen and eats a third of the birthday cake, three days short of winning her no-sugar bet.
Lionel slips downstairs, takes the camera from the mantel and goes out the front door.
From the kitchen window, Dot sees a flashlight crossing to the woodshed and takes it for Rafe.

In the woodshed Lionel can't get the camera's baseplate off in the dark. He sets his reading glasses on the chopping block, gives up and hides the camera in an apple crate. Wren sees the woodshed light come on.
Dot, Wren and finally Lionel are all back inside.

At breakfast Lionel can't find his reading glasses and borrows Bea's spare pair. A third of the cake is gone and Rafe has sawdust on his sleeves. At 4pm Wren fetches kindling and sees Lionel's glasses on the chopping block.
Rafe works on the rocker in the woodshed until just before midnight.
Juno, who borrowed Wren's tote for her songbook, hangs it in the mudroom empty and lies awake in the bunk room until 3. Wren sleeps through.
Lionel creeps down the stairs, which Juno hears, and slips the camera's empty leather case into Wren's tote.
Rafe carries the mended rocker back to the porch.
Bea goes out to look at the stars and finds the rocker back in its place.

Lionel fetches his glasses from the chopping block and finally gets the baseplate off. Then he thinks of Bea's party on that roll, can't bring himself to open it to the light, and puts the camera back in the crate.
Dot goes back down for more cake.

I went for my gardening gloves and found my camera's leather case. In the mudroom. In Wren's tote.
WHAT. i did not put that there!! juno had my tote last night
Also someone crept down the stairs at like 2am?? I heard the creaky step!!

the lake is SO pretty today, I might write a song about it 🎶
ok who was in the woodshed last night. somebody cleared off the whole chopping block

It's Monday. Can we please find the camera.
Last day, everyone. Whatever happens, thank you for coming. Truly.
🥹🥹 love you Bea
A pileated woodpecker at dawn. A fine farewell, I'd say.

guests.name: Bea Lindqvist
guests.role: Your host, the birthday girl, and the camera's owner
guests.voice: Warm and wordy, a retired newspaper photographer. Calls people 'dear', strings thoughts together with dashes, and drops into ALL CAPS when something upsets her.

topics.description: where Bea was and when she went to bed on Friday night, the night the camera vanished

variants.text: I went up at half eleven, dear, and slept like the dead until nearly seven. Sixty takes it out of you.
Bed at 11:30 - I didn't stir until almost seven. Some detective's assistant I'd make.

topics.description: where Bea was and whether she heard anything on Saturday night

variants.text: Tonight? Ask me tomorrow, dear - I'm hoping for a full night's sleep for once.
Saturday night hasn't happened yet! Ask me in the morning.
I slept straight through, I'm ashamed to say. Didn't hear a thing.
Out like a light all Saturday night - whatever went on, I missed it.

topics.description: where Bea was on Sunday night, including her stargazing out on the porch

variants.text: Sunday night? We'll see, dear! Ask me Monday.
Ask me tomorrow - I might sit out and look at the stars if it's clear.
I sat out on the porch looking at the stars from about twenty to eleven until just after eleven. Then bed.
Porch, 10:40 to 11:05 or so, wrapped in a blanket with the stars. Then straight up to bed.

topics.description: the missing camera itself: what it is, where Bea left it and when she found it gone

variants.text: My old rangefinder - thirty years at the Ledger with me. I set it on the mantel after the group photo at half ten, and at seven on Saturday the mantel was EMPTY.
It sat on the mantel from the 10:30 group photo onward - I put it there myself. When I came down at seven it was gone. Just gone.

topics.description: the undeveloped roll of film still inside the camera and which pictures are on it

variants.text: The whole of Friday is on that roll, dear - my sunset walk, dinner, the cake, the group photo at half ten. Twenty-four frames I'll never get back.
Everything from Friday. The sunset on the dock path right through to the group photo. If someone opens the back in daylight, it's all gone.

topics.description: Bea's sunset walk on Friday evening down the dock path, and who she photographed out there

variants.text: Oh, it was glorious. And I got Lionel up a stepladder at the big pine, a perfect silhouette against the sunset - heaven knows what he was doing up there.
I shot the sunset off the dock path. Caught Lionel halfway up a stepladder at the big pine, of all things! I can't wait to see that one printed.

topics.description: Bea's sixtieth birthday dinner on Friday: the toast, the music and the group photo by the fire

variants.text: Juno sang, Dot pretended not to cry, and we finished with a group photo by the fire at half ten. Then the camera went on the mantel.
A perfect night, dear. Last thing I did was the group photo at 10:30, and I set the camera on the mantel right after.

topics.description: the camera's leather case that Bea found in Wren's tote bag in the mudroom on Sunday morning

variants.text: The leather case? What about it, dear?
I'm not sure I follow, dear.
I went to the mudroom for my gardening gloves on Sunday morning and there was my camera's leather case, poking out of Wren's tote. I don't know WHAT to think.
Wren's tote, in the mudroom, Sunday morning - my camera's case, just sitting there. Empty. I can't believe it of her. I won't.

topics.description: the strange goings-on of Sunday night, like the porch rocker reappearing mended

variants.text: Sunday night? Nothing's happened yet, dear, give it time.
Ask me Monday!
When I went out at twenty to eleven, the old rocker was BACK on the porch - mended, good as new! Somebody has a guilty conscience.
The rocker! Gone since Friday, and at 10:40 on Sunday there it was in its place on the porch, glued and sanded. Who DOES that?

topics.description: the lodge's antique porch rocking chair that disappeared on Friday afternoon

variants.text: The lodge's antique rocker has been missing from the porch since Friday afternoon. The owner will have my head.
Gone from the porch since Friday afternoon! Who steals a ROCKING CHAIR?
It came back! I found it on the porch at 10:40 on Sunday night, mended. I'm choosing not to ask.
Back on the porch when I went out for the stars at 10:40 on Sunday - mended, polished, the lot. I could cry.

topics.description: the leftover birthday cake in the kitchen that someone ate a third of overnight

variants.text: A third of my birthday cake vanished on Friday night! It can't be Dot - she's bet me fifty dollars she'll go a month without sugar.
Somebody ate a third of the cake overnight. Not Dot, mind - fifty dollars says she's off sugar for the month.

topics.description: Lionel's lost reading glasses and the spare pair Bea lent him at breakfast

variants.text: Lionel couldn't find his reading glasses at Saturday breakfast, poor man, so I lent him my spare pair. He looks like a startled owl in them.
He lost his specs somewhere on Friday - at breakfast he was squinting at the bird book, so I gave him my spares.

topics.description: Lionel, Bea's neighbor in town and the birding society man, and his famous owl

variants.text: Lionel's my neighbor in town. He's terribly excited - next week he presents the great gray owl he spotted in the big pine here to the birding society.
Dear Lionel. All he talks about is his great gray owl in the big pine - he's presenting it to the birding society next week.

topics.description: Wren, Bea's niece the photography student, and Bea's promise to leave her the camera

variants.text: Wren's my niece - she's studying photography, I taught her on that very camera. I've promised she'll have it one day. Not THIS day.
My Wren. The camera's hers when I'm gone, I've always said so. She knows she only has to wait.

topics.description: Dot, Bea's prickly older sister, and her bet about giving up sugar

variants.text: My big sister. All bark. She's bet me fifty dollars she can go a month without sugar - she's nearly there, too.
Dot's Dot. Sharp as a tack. She's off sugar this month for a fifty-dollar bet with me.

topics.description: Rafe, Bea's old reporter colleague from the Pine County Ledger

variants.text: Rafe wrote the stories, I shot them - twenty years at the Ledger. He's a soft old thing under all that grumbling.
My old partner in crime from the paper. Hates a fuss. Loves a puzzle.

topics.description: Juno, Bea's goddaughter, the folk singer who sang at the party

variants.text: My goddaughter! She sang for me on Friday and I wept like a baby.
Juno is pure sunshine, dear. That voice!

topics.description: the woodshed out back by the lake path, and whether Bea goes in there

variants.text: The woodshed? I haven't set foot in it all weekend, dear. Spiders the size of saucers.
Not my territory. I leave the firewood to the others.
Me? It's MY camera, dear. I'd sooner lose an arm.
Steal my own camera? From my own mantel? On my own BIRTHDAY?

dodges: Oh, I really couldn't say, dear.
Hmm, you'd have to ask one of the others.
I'm all in a muddle today, sorry.
greetings: Hello, dear! Thank you for coming - I'm beside myself.
thanks: Anything, dear. Just find my camera.
dictionary.goodnight: I'm off to bed, dear. Ask me in the morning.

guests.name: Lionel Marsh
guests.role: Bea's neighbor in town, and the county birding society's most decorated member
guests.voice: Courtly and a little pompous. Full sentences, proper punctuation, birdwatching metaphors, 'I'm afraid' and 'dear me'. Melts at any compliment about his birding.

topics.description: where Lionel was and when he slept on Friday night, the night the camera vanished

variants.text: I said my goodnights at twenty to eleven and was asleep by a quarter to. I didn't stir until the dawn chorus.
Upstairs at 10:40 and asleep by 10:45, I'm afraid. An early bird must roost early. Not a peep from me until dawn.

topics.description: where Lionel was on Saturday night and whether he got up

variants.text: Tonight? An early roost, I should think. Ask me in the morning.
The night is young, detective. Ask me tomorrow.
I slept straight through, I'm pleased to say. Not so much as a creak.
Dead to the world all Saturday night. The lake air, you know.

topics.description: where Lionel was on Sunday night and when he went up

variants.text: Sunday night is still ahead of us, detective. Patience is the birder's first virtue.
Ask me on Monday, if you would.
I went up at a quarter to ten and didn't come down until morning. Dull, I'm afraid, but true.
Upstairs by 9:45 with a field guide. I didn't come down again until breakfast.

topics.description: Bea's missing camera, where it was kept and when Lionel last saw it

variants.text: Bea set it on the mantel after the group photograph at half past ten. That's the last I saw of it.
On the mantel, after the 10:30 photograph. A handsome old thing. Dreadful business.

topics.description: the undeveloped film inside the camera and what pictures might be on it

variants.text: I couldn't tell you what's on it. Cake and candles, I'd imagine.
Film, I gather. I don't follow photography. Birds don't sit still for it.

topics.description: Lionel on Friday evening at sunset: the dock path, the big pine, a stepladder, and whether Bea took his photo

variants.text: Bea didn't take a single photograph of me on Friday, I'm quite sure. I keep well clear of cameras. I don't photograph well.
A photograph of me? Not on Friday, no. I made a point of keeping out of her viewfinder.

topics.description: the woodshed out back and whether Lionel has been inside it

variants.text: The woodshed? I haven't set foot in it all weekend. Spiders, detective. I draw the line at spiders.
Never been inside it. Firewood is a young man's game.

topics.description: Lionel's own tortoiseshell reading glasses, losing them, and the spare pair Bea lent him

variants.text: Mislaid, I'm afraid. Bea very kindly lent me her spare pair at Saturday breakfast.
Lost them somewhere. Bea took pity on me at breakfast and lent me hers. Rather too pink for my taste.
Found them, thank goodness. I have my own glasses back. Panic over.
Oh, they turned up. Back on my nose where they belong.

topics.description: the camera's leather case turning up in Wren's tote bag in the mudroom

variants.text: I'm afraid I don't follow, detective.
A tote? I couldn't say.
A sorry business. Bea found her camera case in young Wren's tote. I take no pleasure in saying it.
In Wren's tote, of all places. One hates to draw conclusions. And yet.

topics.description: the noises and goings-on of Sunday night: the cleared chopping block, the rocker coming back

variants.text: Nothing has happened yet, surely?
Let's see what the night brings.
Raccoons, I expect. I heard nothing. I was upstairs by a quarter to ten.
I was in bed by 9:45 and stayed there. Whatever went bump, it wasn't me.

topics.description: Lionel's great gray owl sighting in the big pine and his talk about it for the birding society

variants.text: Ah! The great gray. In the big pine, right here at Pine Hollow. I present it to the county birding society next week. Quite the coup.
A great gray owl in the big pine, detective. Next week the birding society hears all about it. I've been practising my slides.

topics.description: the other birds Lionel has seen at the lake this weekend, and his skill as a birder

variants.text: A pair of loons, a kingfisher and, if I'm not mistaken, a pileated woodpecker. Not a bad weekend's list.
Kind of you to ask! Loons on the water at dawn. Nothing on earth like it.

topics.description: Lionel's own phone and what the Wi-Fi log shows it doing at night

variants.text: My nephew set the wretched thing up. I couldn't tell you what it gets up to at night.
I barely know how to answer it, detective. A log of what, exactly?

topics.description: Bea's birthday dinner on Friday night, the group photo, and when Lionel left it

variants.text: A lovely evening. The group photograph at half ten, the camera on the mantel, and I said goodnight at twenty to eleven.
Delightful. I stayed for the 10:30 photograph and was upstairs by 10:40. Early riser.

topics.description: Bea, the host, Lionel's neighbor in town

variants.text: Bea is the dearest neighbor a man could ask for. This has upset her terribly.
Twelve years next door to Bea. She waters my ferns. I'd do anything for her.

topics.description: Wren, Bea's niece the photography student, and her interest in the camera

variants.text: Young Wren has had her eye on that camera all weekend. I say nothing more.
A photography student, I gather. Very keen on that camera. Very keen indeed.
Bea found her camera case in Wren's tote, you know. I take no pleasure in it.
Her tote, detective. Bea's camera case was in Wren's tote. I'm only repeating what's known.

topics.description: Dot, Bea's sharp-tongued older sister

variants.text: Dorothy is... bracing. Like a north wind off the lake.
She told me my owl slides were 'a lot'. I've decided to take it as a compliment.

topics.description: Rafe, the retired newspaperman who used to work with Bea

variants.text: A newspaperman. They do like poking about where they oughtn't.
Rafe? Quiet sort. Asks a great many questions for a man who answers so few.

topics.description: Juno, Bea's goddaughter the singer

variants.text: Juno sings like a hermit thrush. I told her so myself.
A delightful girl. A touch loud before breakfast.
I beg your pardon! I am a birder, detective, not a burglar. If you want someone with an eye on that camera, ask young Wren.
Dear me. Is this how you treat all your witnesses? I suggest you look a little closer to Bea's family.
Really, this is beneath you. Ask Wren how Bea's camera case came to be in her tote.
I am seventy-one years old and I identify warblers for pleasure. The case was in WREN's tote, detective.

dodges: You'd do better to ask Bea.
That's rather outside my field, detective.
I make it a rule not to speculate.
greetings: Good day, detective. A fine morning for it.
Ah, detective. How can I help?
thanks: Not at all, not at all.
dictionary.goodnight: I'm off to roost, detective. Ask me in the morning.

guests.name: Dot Fairweather
guests.voice: Dry and terse. Short sentences with full stops, even on questions. No emoji, ever. Sarcasm is her love language.

topics.description: where Dot was on Friday night, the night the camera vanished, and whether she came downstairs

variants.text: In bed by ten. I didn't come down again. I'm sixty-four, not sixteen.
Bed at ten. Stayed there. Riveting, I know.

topics.description: where Dot was on Saturday night

variants.text: Asleep. Assuming the rest of you let me.
Ask me tomorrow.
Asleep. Earplugs in. Didn't hear a thing.
Slept through. Earplugs. Best investment I ever made.

topics.description: where Dot was on Sunday night and whether she came downstairs

variants.text: Ask me Monday.
It hasn't happened yet. Patience.
Bed by ten. Never came down. Same as every night.
In bed at ten and stayed there. Shocking, I know.

topics.description: Bea's missing camera and where it was left on Friday

variants.text: Bea says she left it on the mantel after her half-ten photo. I'd gone up by then.
On the mantel at 10:30, apparently. She leaves things everywhere. It was bound to happen.

topics.description: the undeveloped film inside the camera and what's on it

variants.text: Pictures of people chewing. Hardly worth stealing.
I don't know what's on it. I made a point of being out of frame.

topics.description: Dot's bet with Bea about giving up sugar, and whether she ate the missing birthday cake

variants.text: I bet Bea fifty dollars I could go a month without sugar. Draw your own conclusions.
A month off sugar. Fifty dollars riding on it. Why would I touch the cake.

topics.description: the woodshed out back and who Dot has seen going in and out of it

variants.text: Around six on Friday I saw Rafe drag something bulky under a tarp into the woodshed. Ask him what.
Rafe. Friday, about six. Hauling something under a tarp into that woodshed. Make of it what you will.

topics.description: the camera's leather case turning up in Wren's tote bag in the mudroom

variants.text: What tote.
I don't follow.
Bea's camera case in the girl's tote. Convenient place for it. Too convenient.
In Wren's tote. In the mudroom. Where anyone could put anything. Think.

topics.description: the goings-on of Sunday night that people noticed on Monday morning

variants.text: Nothing has happened. Yet.
Ask me Monday.
I sleep at night. Unlike some people in this house.
Ask the night owls. I'm not one.

topics.description: Dot's own phone and what the Wi-Fi log shows about it in the kitchen at night

variants.text: I don't understand that log and I don't intend to.
My phone is a phone. It does what it likes.

topics.description: Bea's birthday dinner on Friday and when Dot left it

variants.text: Too loud. Too much singing. I was in bed by ten and stayed there.
Nice enough. I left them to it and was in bed by ten. Never came back down.

topics.description: the lodge's antique porch rocker that went missing on Friday

variants.text: Gone from the porch since Friday afternoon. I have my theories.
Missing since Friday afternoon. Somebody sat in it who shouldn't have. That's all I'll say in public.

topics.description: Bea, Dot's younger sister and the host

variants.text: My baby sister. Sixty, and still can't keep track of her things.
Bea trusts everybody. That's her problem.

topics.description: Lionel, Bea's birdwatching neighbor

variants.text: Lionel. Talks about owls like they owe him money.
He showed me forty slides of a blurry owl. I counted.

topics.description: Wren, Dot's niece the photography student

variants.text: The girl's been mooning over that camera since she was twelve. Doesn't make her a thief.
Wren. Lovely. Exhausting. Never off that phone.

topics.description: Rafe, Bea's old newspaper colleague, and what Dot saw him hauling

variants.text: Rafe dragged something under a tarp into the woodshed around six on Friday. Ask him what. I did. He changed the subject.
Watch Rafe. Friday at six he was hauling something bulky into the woodshed under a tarp.

topics.description: Juno, Bea's goddaughter the singer

variants.text: Juno. Sweet girl. Sings at breakfast. Someone should stop her.
Talented. Loud. Apologizes too much.

I did not take Bea's camera. If you must know, I was in the kitchen at one in the morning eating her birthday cake. And around ten past one I saw a flashlight going out to the woodshed. I assumed it was Rafe.
Fine. I came down at quarter to one and ate a third of the cake. There goes fifty dollars. While I was at it, a flashlight crossed the yard to the woodshed around 1:10. Happy.

dictionary.goodnight: I'm going to bed. Don't text me.

guests.name: Rafe Okonjo
guests.role: Bea's old reporter colleague from the Pine County Ledger
guests.voice: Clipped, like a man still writing to a word count. Fragments. Full stops. Often answers a question with a question.

topics.description: where Rafe was on Friday night, the night the camera vanished

variants.text: Upstairs at eleven. Book. Lights out. Why?
Went up at eleven. Read. Slept.

topics.description: where Rafe was on Saturday night and whether he left his room

variants.text: Haven't decided. Ask tomorrow.
Tonight? Early, probably.
Turned in at eleven. Stayed in my room. All night.
Eleven. Bed. Didn't leave the room. Next.

topics.description: where Rafe was on Sunday night and when he went to bed

variants.text: Ask me Monday.
Hasn't happened yet. Come back tomorrow.
Bed around half eleven. Long day.
Turned in about 11:30. That's it.

topics.description: Bea's missing camera, its history and when Rafe last saw it

variants.text: That camera shot every front page I wrote. Last saw it going on the mantel after the 10:30 photo.
On the mantel. After the half-ten group shot. Then I went up.

topics.description: the undeveloped film inside the camera and why someone might want it gone

variants.text: Whatever's on that roll, somebody doesn't want it printed. That's my read.
Nobody steals a sixty-year-old camera for resale. They steal it for the film. Ask what's on it.

topics.description: the woodshed out back and whether Rafe has been inside it

variants.text: Haven't been near it all weekend. Why?
The woodshed? Not once. Not my department.

topics.description: the lodge's antique porch rocker that went missing on Friday and who broke it

variants.text: Missing since Friday afternoon, I hear. Not my beat.
Gone from the porch since Friday. Ask the owner. Rockers break.
Heard it turned up. Good. No story.
It's back? Then drop it.

topics.description: Lionel's great gray owl sighting and whether Rafe believes it

variants.text: Great grays don't come this far south. I checked. Nobody's ever logged one near Pine Hollow. Except Lionel.
Off the record? I don't buy it. Great gray this far south, no other sighting on record. Smells.

topics.description: the camera's leather case turning up in Wren's tote bag in the mudroom

variants.text: What case?
Don't know anything about a tote.
Case in the niece's tote. Too neat. Plants usually are.
Wren's tote, mudroom, Sunday morning. Anyone could reach that hook. Who'd want us looking at Wren?

topics.description: what happened on Sunday night and whether Rafe noticed anything

variants.text: Nothing yet. Ask me Monday.
Night's not over. Patience.
Turned in at half eleven. Missed whatever it was.
Asleep from 11:30. Nothing to report.

topics.description: Rafe's own phone and the woodshed entries for him in the Wi-Fi log

variants.text: Logs don't lie. People read them wrong.
A phone isn't a person. Ever think of that?

topics.description: Bea's birthday dinner on Friday, the group photo, and when Rafe went up

variants.text: Good party. Group photo at 10:30, camera to the mantel, I went up at eleven.
Toast, cake, Juno sang. Photo at half ten, camera on the mantel. Bed at eleven.

topics.description: Rafe and Bea's twenty years together at the Pine County Ledger newspaper

variants.text: Twenty years. She shot, I wrote. Best photographer the Ledger ever had.
The Ledger? Folded in '09. We were the last two out the door.

topics.description: Bea, the host, Rafe's old colleague

variants.text: Bea's the real thing. Don't let the chatter fool you.
Known her thirty years. She'd give you the coat off her back. Then photograph you in it.

topics.description: Lionel, the birdwatching neighbor, and Rafe's doubts about his owl

variants.text: Lionel. Ask him about his owl. Great grays don't come this far south. No other record near here. Ever.
Nice man. Shaky story. A great gray at Pine Hollow, and not one other birder ever logged one nearby?

topics.description: Wren, Bea's niece the photography student

variants.text: Bright kid. Wants that camera. Doesn't make her a thief.
Wren? Talks a lot. Hides nothing. Thieves are quieter.

topics.description: Dot, Bea's sharp older sister

variants.text: Dot watches everything. Says half.
Sharp. Would've made a good editor.

topics.description: Juno, Bea's goddaughter the singer

variants.text: Juno. Good voice. Nervous as a cat.
Can't keep a secret to save her life. Useful, for you.
I didn't take the camera. Fine. Off the record. I broke the lodge's rocker Friday afternoon. Been mending it in the woodshed so nobody'd know. That's the whole story.
You want a confession? Here. I sat in that antique rocker Friday and it folded. I've been fixing it in the woodshed. I didn't touch Bea's camera.

guests.name: Juno Reyes
guests.voice: Bubbly and breathless. Proper capitals but lots of exclamation marks, double question marks and ✨🎶. Lights up when anyone mentions her singing.

topics.description: where Juno was on Friday night, the night the camera vanished, and when she went to bed

variants.text: Wren and I jammed by the fire till 12:30 and the camera was still on the mantel then!! I got a glass of water and was in bed by 12:40 ✨
Music with Wren till 12:30 - camera still on the mantel! Water from the kitchen, bed by 12:40!

topics.description: where Juno was on Saturday night, practicing in the sunroom and lying awake in the bunk room

variants.text: Tonight I'm practicing in the sunroom!! 🎶 Ask me tomorrow!
Ask me in the morning!! I'll probably be up late singing, sorry in advance!
At 1:50 I hung Wren's tote in the mudroom - totally empty, I'd just taken my songbook out!! Then I lay awake in the bunk room till 3 and Wren never moved once!
Sunroom, then at 1:50 I hung Wren's tote up EMPTY in the mudroom, then bunk room. Couldn't sleep till 3! Wren was out cold the whole time!!

topics.description: where Juno was on Sunday night

variants.text: Ask me tomorrow!! ✨
Hasn't happened yet, silly!
Asleep by 11:30 and slept all night for once!! 😴
Out like a light at 11:30! Didn't hear a single thing, sorry!!

topics.description: Bea's missing camera and when Juno last saw it on the mantel

variants.text: It was definitely still on the mantel at 12:30 when Wren and I stopped playing!! I looked right at it!
12:30 on Friday night, on the mantel, I'd swear to it!! 🥺

topics.description: the undeveloped film inside the camera and the pictures on it

variants.text: Bea took SO many pictures of me singing!! If that roll's ruined I'll cry.
My whole set is on that roll probably!! 😭

topics.description: the camera's leather case found in Wren's tote bag, which Juno had borrowed

variants.text: Wren's tote? Um, what about it??
I don't know anything about a tote, sorry!!
Wren lent me her tote Saturday for my songbook! I hung it in the mudroom at 1:50 and there was NOTHING else in it!! And Wren never left her bunk after, I was awake till 3!
It was MY fault it was in the mudroom!! I borrowed it from Wren, emptied it, hung it up at 1:50 with nothing inside. Wren slept the whole time, I was awake till 3!!

topics.description: the footsteps Juno heard creeping down the stairs in the middle of Saturday night

variants.text: The stairs? The third one creaks!! That's all I know!
Um, they're stairs? 🎶
Around 2:05 I heard someone creep down the stairs!! The creaky third step! I was too scared to look 🙈
Somebody went down the stairs at like 2:05!! Super slow, like they didn't want to be heard!

topics.description: what happened on Sunday night and whether Juno heard any of it

variants.text: Nothing's happened yet!! Ask me Monday!
Tomorrow!! ✨
I slept right through it all, I was asleep by 11:30!! So sorry!!
No idea, I was asleep by 11:30 for once!! 😴

topics.description: Friday evening before dinner, the sunset, and what Juno saw someone carrying up from the dock path

variants.text: Ooh! Around 7:45 on Friday I saw Lionel coming up from the dock path with a stepladder and a lumpy pillowcase?? Very mysterious ✨
Lionel!! Friday about 7:45, hurrying up from the dock path with a stepladder and a pillowcase with something lumpy in it!

topics.description: the birthday cake in the kitchen and the big piece missing on Saturday morning

variants.text: Someone ate a THIRD of the birthday cake overnight!! I went to make Bea breakfast Saturday and it was just... gone!
A whole third of the cake, gone by Saturday morning!! Not me, I swear, I'm a savory person!

topics.description: the lodge's antique porch rocker that went missing on Friday

variants.text: The old rocker's been missing from the porch since Friday afternoon!! I loved that chair!
Gone since Friday afternoon!! Who takes a rocking chair??

topics.description: Bea's birthday party on Friday, Juno's song, and the group photo

variants.text: I sang Bea a song I wrote for her and she CRIED!! Then the group photo at 10:30 and the camera went on the mantel!
Best night!! Group photo by the fire at 10:30, then Bea put the camera on the mantel ✨

topics.description: compliments about Juno's singing, her songs and her music career

variants.text: Stop!! Do you really think so?? 🥹✨
Oh my gosh, thank you!! I have an EP coming out in spring!!

topics.description: Juno's own phone and the kitchen entries for her in the Wi-Fi log

variants.text: The kitchen on Friday is me getting a glass of water before bed!! Bed by 12:40, promise!
That's just me getting water on Friday!! I was in bed by 12:40!
Friday's kitchen one is me getting water, bed by 12:40! And Saturday's is me at 1:50 hanging Wren's tote up in the mudroom, EMPTY!
Water on Friday, bed by 12:40! Then Saturday at 1:50 I was hanging Wren's empty tote in the mudroom! Nothing sneaky, promise!!

topics.description: Bea, Juno's godmother and the host

variants.text: Bea is my godmother and the best person alive!! I hate seeing her sad 🥺
She bought me my first guitar!! I'd do anything for her!

topics.description: Lionel, the birdwatching neighbor, and what Juno saw him carrying on Friday

variants.text: Lionel's so sweet!! Oh - on Friday around 7:45 I saw him coming up from the dock path with a stepladder and a lumpy pillowcase? Birdwatching stuff maybe??
He said I sing like a thrush!! 🥹 Also he was carrying a stepladder and a lumpy pillowcase up from the dock path at like 7:45 Friday, which was weird??

topics.description: Wren, Juno's bunkmate, and whether Wren could have hidden the camera case

variants.text: Wren's my bunkmate!! She'd never, she adores Bea!
Wren is a sweetheart, she just talks a LOT 😅
It can't be Wren!! I hung her tote up empty at 1:50 and lay awake till 3 and she didn't move once!
Not Wren!! Her tote was empty when I hung it up at 1:50, and she was asleep till way after 3, I was lying right there awake!

topics.description: Dot, Bea's prickly older sister

variants.text: Dot pretends she hates my singing but she hummed along on Friday!! 🎶
Dot scares me a little but in a good way??

topics.description: Rafe, Bea's quiet old reporter friend, and the sawdust on his sleeves

variants.text: Rafe is SO mysterious!! He came to Saturday breakfast with sawdust all over his sleeves?? Like a lumberjack!
Rafe's nice! Quiet! He had sawdust on his sleeves at Saturday breakfast, I don't know why!!
Me?? Oh no no no. I was in bed by 12:40, I promise!! 😭
I would NEVER!! I got water and went to bed at 12:40, ask anyone!!
No!! I was in bed by 12:40 on Friday! And Saturday I hung Wren's tote up EMPTY at 1:50, I'm not lying!! 😭
I didn't do anything!! Bed at 12:40 Friday, and Saturday I hung Wren's tote up at 1:50 with nothing in it! 🥺

dodges: That's a Bea question, I think!
greetings: Oh hi!! How can I help??
dictionary.goodnight: Okay I'm going to bed!! Night night ✨
